facts.text: Buffers MLX allocates (not no-copy wraps) and fills by GPU eval are charged to phys_footprint in full. A 60-iteration loop of ~500 MB alloc, eval, drop left 60.19 GB footprint, which matched active + cache within 0.14 GB.
Freed MLX buffers stay in the allocator pool, remain live Metal allocations and stay in phys_footprint; get_peak_memory tracks only active memory.
clear_cache returns memory but phys_footprint trails the call by about 4 seconds (15.14 GB immediately, 0.02 GB at the next sample).
A first reading right after clear_cache looked like a leak and was retracted by its author as a sampling artifact.
Real incidents: a hard reboot and a Metal command-buffer GPU timeout on M5 Max 128 GB when the gate used get_peak_memory (46 GB reported, 110 GB real).
A commenter reports a kernel panic (watchdogd 90 s timeout, 123.2 GiB resident, 50.1 GiB compressor) running Ollama 0.33.x MLX on an M5 Max 128 GB.
GPU-written MLX allocator buffers are charged to phys_footprint as IOAccelerator (graphics) dirty memory.
A 60 x 500 MB churn showed get_peak_memory 1.00 GB, active 0, cache 60.06 GB, footprint 60.19 GB.
With cache_limit=0 the same churn ended at 1.14 GB footprint.
The pool reuse window is [size, size + 2 pages), so varying request sizes grow the pool (cited as mlx issue 3886).
The mlx maintainer's position: get_peak_memory is for single-model runs where cache hit rate is near 100 percent; for long-running or parallel serving use active + cache.
After clear_cache, phys_footprint falls over a few seconds, not instantly.

CONTRADICTS (partly): iokit-mapped-metal-buffer-accounting-in-phys-foo.md measured a GPU-blit-filled untouched no-copy region at 0.12 GB footprint. Here GPU-written MLX-allocated buffers (not no-copy wraps) are charged in full as IOAccelerator dirty memory. The difference is plausibly allocation type (device allocation vs wrapped anonymous pages), but no source tests a GPU-written no-copy buffer directly.
